readout: All four smoke/4K runs satisfy exact saved endpoint and gain-history checks. Each 4K run has 39 extra forwards and all three no-op replays are exact. CR15 remains failed under its original policy.

Axial octave half-step responses are small and poorly predicted: most errors are near the zero-change predictor; some exceed it. Counts below one are descriptive and are not statistical evidence of reliable control.

The scalar control is better predicted at middle and late sampled steps, but prompt 0 step 6 fails strongly. Late scalar relative errors are 0.10423 and 0.04982. This is prompt/time dependent rather than a universal positive response law.

Scalar changes generally increase measured band powers; axial responses include many negative components and substantial responses on the other output axis. Weak prediction and coarse marginal spectra prevent interpreting this as a validated controllability map.

The same epsilon does not give the scalar and octave controls the same actuator norm. Effect magnitude alone cannot rank intrinsic actuator efficiency; row records include effect divided by realized BF16 logit-gain norm.

Exploratory realized-coordinate refitting changes most prediction errors only modestly. Half-step BF16 actuator vectors are substantially off the full-step secant line for octave controls. A one-coordinate amplitude correction cannot identify or explain their orthogonal response.

The derivative statistic concerns packed-latent marginal log power of x_t-sigma*v. It is neither final pixel frequency power nor perceptual quality. No perturbed trajectory was selected or decoded as efficacy evidence.
limits: Two already used development prompts, one seed, one backbone and three directions; no confidence interval, generalization, fresh 64-prompt confirmation, or SOTA claim.
Three tested controls do not identify reachable and unreachable spectral-error subspaces. High cross-axis fraction does not establish that off-diagonal feedback helps.
Nominal finite differences traverse a normalized gain path, with BF16 gain and network arithmetic. They are local secants, not an exact infinitesimal Jacobian of a smooth FP32 model.
A negative directional derivative is not inherently wrong-sign control: that conclusion additionally requires a justified desired error direction, which this probe does not provide.
Quantization off-linearity is measured, but its causal share of prediction failure is not identified. Network nonlinearity, normalization curvature, and BF16 activation arithmetic remain confounded.
Baseline/probed runtime difference is diagnostic accounting with unmatched warmup and no image decoding, not production speed or equal-cost efficacy evidence.
Deterministic allocation changes numerical execution policy; CR16 evidence does not establish quality equivalence to the original released baseline at 4K.

next_bounded_experiment_recommendation.status: Recommendation only; no job or source change authorized by this report
next_bounded_experiment_recommendation.immediate_action: Keep the realized-coordinate calculation as a labeled secondary CPU analysis. Do not expand the response matrix or build a full spectral-feedback controller from these 18 rows.
next_bounded_experiment_recommendation.if_further_gpu_diagnosis_is_chosen: Freeze a small perturbation-scale test at step 14 on the same two development prompts, same checkpoint/schedule and three controls. Measure +/-0.20,+/-0.10,+/-0.05; fit at 0.20 and predict 0.10, then fit at 0.10 and predict 0.05 as separately declared comparisons. Repeat one half-positive intervention per control to check repeatability. Retain exact no-op/history/endpoint checks and save all realized FP32/BF16 gains.
next_bounded_experiment_recommendation.max_forward_budget: 78 per prompt,156 total: two 28-step baseline/probed trajectories plus 18 perturbation calls,3 duplicated half-positive calls, and 1 unperturbed replay per prompt. This is a bounded diagnostic rather than a quality campaign.
next_bounded_experiment_recommendation.decision_use: Inspect whether a perturbation window produces consistent directional prediction beyond zero after accounting for actual actuator geometry. Preserve a negative result. A positive result would justify another response-control test, not held-out efficacy or a novelty claim.
next_bounded_experiment_recommendation.prior_art_boundary: Local novelty notes flag SEGA content-adaptive RoPE gains, spectral-reference guidance, and existing finite-difference/trust-region/control methods. Finite differences, scalar temperature control, or numerical determinism alone are not a new mechanism. A later proposal must show why a resolution-specific response mechanism adds value beyond scalar, sign-free and diagonal/equal-cost controls.
next_bounded_experiment_recommendation.prior_art_verification_scope: Used existing project notes as boundaries; did not conduct a new literature search or establish novelty.
